messages:
ryan: heads-up — dashboard alerted: hosted-usw2 p95 queueing climbed to 4.2s, admission control started shedding low-priority slots at 11:02 UTC :rotating_light:
alert-bot: [ALERT] gpu-pool-utilization-hosted-usw2 > 92% for 5m — link: https://dash.redwood.internal/hosted-usw2/slot-heatmap
maya: seeing the same heatmap tailspike on 'slot tail utilization' — looks localized to pool-7, post-warmup seqLen heavy workloads :thinking_face:
elaine: any concurrent deploys or model rollouts in that region? canary traffic?
kevin: no deploys flagged. infra autoscaler shows refill failing on 2 nodes (provision timeout 300s). logs: ```provisioner: aws-ec2 timeout waiting for instance bootstrap```
tara: curious — eviction rate ticked up too? that would amplify admission pressure if KV cache misses spike.
ryan: yeah eviction rate jumped from 0.6% -> 3.4% after 10:58, KV cache miss rate correlates with the same timeframe. probable cold-start churn + a burst of long-seqlen inference.
kevin: opened an infra ticket to repro provisioning failures, tagging @sre-oncall. ticket: INF-7352.
sre-oncall: hopping in. immediate actions: 1) reduce batch targets for pool-7 to buy headroom 2) enable regional fallback to eus2 for low-tier customers 3) bump canary throttle to 30%
maya: I pushed a temporary admission tweak: lowered per-slot concurrent limit from 6 -> 4 for pool-7. watching p95 now.
alert-bot: [INFO] admission-policy-change applied by maya — per-slot-limit=4 on pool-7
elaine: can we also flip on prefix cache warming for the top 50 customers? might help KV miss storm. who owns that script?
ryan: that'd be kevin — kevin, can you run warming job for top50 in hosted-usw2? quick command: ```./tools/cache_warm --region usw2 --customers top50 --concurrency 8```
kevin: starting the warming job now. ETA ~6m. also increasing provisioner retry from 3 -> 5 to reduce transient timeouts.
tara: good. cost note: if we keep fallback to eus2 for sustained period we start incurring cross-region egress and higher unit cost — flagging for finance if SLA hits persist.
sre-oncall: monitoring. if p95 doesn't drop under 1.2s in 10m we execute spillover to eus2 for staged traffic. who's on postmortem if this becomes recurring? ryan?/elaine?
ryan: i'll lead the postmortem with kevin and maya. will capture provisioning timeouts, cache-miss churn, and potential routing policy gaps.
elaine: adding runbook checklist to the ticket: bootstrapping healthchecks, cache warming, admission tuning, fallback thresholds, cost triggers.
kevin: warming job done. KV miss rate down ~28% in the last 2m. p95 now 1.1s and admission queues shrinking :thumbsup:
maya: nice — reverting per-slot limit to 5 to balance throughput.
sre-oncall: great. leaving monitoring on for 30m, adding automated alert to page at 3m sustained >85% pool util next time.
ryan: thanks everyone. action items in INF-7352: kevin(provisioner retries + postmortem), maya(admission tuning notes), ryan(postmortem owner), elaine(runbook updates).
kevin: note for postmortem — suggest we surface 'provision success latency' on the dashboard next to headroom so we can correlate faster.
elaine: agreed. also add a small visualization for cross-region fallback cost impact.
alert-bot: [RESOLVED] gpu-pool-utilization-hosted-usw2 back to 78% — alert cleared.
ryan: closing thread — will sync in weekly ops review with dashboards adjustments. :white_check_mark:
